situation:
You are the regional human resources manager at KESTREL LODGING GROUP, a hotel management company that operates twenty-two properties across four states. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to meet this morning about the way employee discipline is being handed out at the company's largest hotels, and to arrive with a recommendation rather than a summary.

KESTREL bought HALLOWFIELD HOSPITALITY eleven months ago and has not finished putting the two companies together. Payroll and benefits were combined last spring, but each side kept the attendance rules it arrived with. Legacy KESTREL hotels still run on a supervisor's judgment and a quiet conversation. The former HALLOWFIELD hotels run on a written point system that records every late arrival.

Both systems now operate inside the same buildings. Housekeepers on the morning shift, most of them former HALLOWFIELD employees, collect points and lose shift preference for arriving ten minutes late. Overnight front desk and laundry staff, many with more than fifteen years at KESTREL, have the same absences settled in a conversation and nothing is written down. Employees compare notes in the break room and see the difference.

Standardizing on the written point system would treat everyone alike, but several long-tenured overnight employees would sit one absence from termination for behavior their supervisors have overlooked for years, and some of them would leave. Standardizing on supervisor judgment would lift that threat, and would tell the morning housekeepers that the points already on their records, and the promotions those points cost them, counted for nothing.

The vice president (judge) wants you to recommend which standard KESTREL should adopt, how the change will be explained to the employees it treats worse, and how supervisors on both sides will be trained to apply it the same way. You will present your recommendation to the vice president (judge), who will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of operations (judge) at KESTREL LODGING GROUP. Business background is the same as the situation above. Eleven months after acquiring HALLOWFIELD HOSPITALITY, the company is running two sets of attendance rules inside the same hotels, and employees on the same floor are being treated differently for the same absence.

You have asked the regional human resources manager to recommend which standard the company should adopt, how the change will be explained to the group of employees it treats worse, and how supervisors on both sides will be trained to apply the standard consistently.

After the participant has presented, ask these questions:
judgeQuestions: Six months after we make this change, what will supervisors be doing differently than they are doing today?
If employees still believe the rule bends by shift a year from now, what will that have cost us?
